reviewer_summary.question: Why can the model process the known prompt together but choose the answer only one token at a time?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: Picking blue does not process it, so the model must feed it back through the layers before choosing and; keeping earlier keys and values saves repeated work.

findings.problem: I lose the concrete example when the six K tags appear. A key supposedly says what a position is relevant to, but I have not seen blue looking for anything yet, or an example of what one earlier position offers it. I cannot connect these new lists to the looking back I previously understood as arrows between words.

resolution.note: Substantial rewrite after R3: show the actual saved numeric pair for The/layer 1, describe its role as an input to new computation; defer the matching formula to optional depth. New fresh review required.

findings.problem: The query is introduced and immediately compared with every allowed key, but the picture shows only arrows. I can see which positions are allowed, but not what blue is looking for or why one earlier position would contribute more than another. That leaves the comparison-to-mixing link in the next beat dependent on an unexplained idea of relevance.

resolution.note: Removed unexplained relevance metaphor and query terminology from core. State exactly which old and new numerical results are consumed; interactive depth shows the actual matching arithmetic. Fresh review required.

findings.problem: With exact arithmetic introduces an unexplained condition during the answer to my prediction. I thought repeating the same calculations would produce the same result; now I wonder whether ordinary calculations might change the answer, and whether my prediction was supposed to account for that.

resolution.note: Rephrased the condition as in this exact toy, repeating the same calculation, preserving the qualification without unexplained floating-point terminology.
